newsitem.title: JAPAN: Olympus unveils pocket-sized digital cameras.
newsitem.headline: Olympus unveils pocket-sized digital cameras.

text.p: Japan's Olympus Optical Co Ltd on Thursday unveiled a pocket-sized high-resolution digital camera.
The Camedia C-820L features an 810,000-pixel charged couple device (CCD), measures 128mm by 65mm by 45mm and weighs approximately 265 grams, Olympus said.
It is the smallest and lightest digital camera with such high-quality images, Olympus said, and comes with a two-inch color liquid-crystal display monitor.
The images are saved on 3.3V SmartMedia cards, which are removable stamp-sized flash-memory storage cards, Olympus said.
The images can be printed out on a P-300 digital colour printer, which was announced along with the camera, it said.
Olympus also unveiled the C-420L digital camera with a 350,000-pixel CCD, which is the same size as the C-820L and weighs approximately 260 grams.
The C-820L will be launched in late July at 84,800 yen and the C-420L will be in stores in early September at 64,800 yen, Olympus said.
Olympus said it expects to produce 15,000 units of each model per month.
Earlier this week, Toshiba Corp unveiled the Allegretto PDR-2, which is smaller than Olympus' new models and uses a 330,000-pixel complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS).
